newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's KGHM shares seen on offer at end Q2 1997.
newsitem.headline: Poland's KGHM shares seen on offer at end Q2 1997.

text.p: Shares in Poland's privatised KGHM copper concern are likely to hit the international and domestic markets at the end of the second quarter of 1997, an official from the consortium arranging the sale said on Wednesday.
The consortium consists of Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS), Barclays de Zoete Wedd and Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy SA brokerage.

Rafal Sosna, head of the UBS corporate finance department in Warsaw told Reuters 15 percent of KGHM's stock will be given to its employees while about 34 percent of the shares would be earmarked for the public.
"The domestic and international share offering of KGHM Polska Miedz will be at the end of the second quarter of 1997," said Sosna.
"The division of the stake into international and domestic tranches will be done after market research," he said.
The state will retain a 51 percent stake in KGHM, one of the world's major copper and silver producers, the value of which is estimated at $2-3 billion.

Earlier this year KGHM's board proposed that since all the cash from the privatisation of the company would go to the treasury's coffers, the concern should issue new shares either with the initial offering or shortly after.
Sosna said the privatising consortium had not yet reviewed the proposal.
"Information on whether there will be a KGHM capital rise will be released in the first quarter of 1997," Sosna said.
He said the copper firms' international offering was likely to be in the form of Global Depositary Receipts (GDR) which would be listed in London.
The domestic offering could be done at a special bourse session, but the final decision would belong to WBK brokerage.
The GDRs would be sold internationally by both UBS and Barclays, which would also fully underwrite the offering at the cost of 2.3 percent of shares sold.
It has not yet been decided whether the consortium would underwrite the domestic offer.
KGHM had a net profit of 481.9 million zlotys last year against 351.1 million in 1994 on sales of 3.72 billion zlotys against 2.69 billion in 1994.
In 1995 KGHM produced 405,739 tonnes of electrolytic copper and 964 tonnes of silver.
It plans to increase its copper output to 470,000 tonnes per year by 2000 while raising its silver output to 1,020 tonnes.
